old: In this guide, subconscious means the deeper processes shaping perception, emotion, desire, avoidance, imagery, memory, bodily signals, habits, intuition, and automatic behavior. Sometimes it helps to address all of that as one mind; sometimes an ecology of parts gives more precision. Both are maps. Neither needs its own priesthood.
Parts give precision. Higher Self gives coherence. Communion is the movement between them.
When you need coherence, speak to the deeper mind as a whole:
“Wise subconscious, please help me understand.”

When you need precision, notice the different tendencies inside it: the child wanting love, the protector wanting safety, the critic wanting standards, the fantasy-maker wanting possibility, the body memory wanting recognition, the social self wanting belonging, the spiritual self wanting God or source or the benefit of all beings, and the wiser part wanting what is true.
Begin with unity when the system feels scattered:
“Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious, please guide me.”
Differentiate only when the question needs it:
“Which part of me is afraid?” “Which part is protecting?” “Which part is avoiding?” “Which part knows the next step?” “Which part is too young to carry this?”
Then bring the parts back into one life:
“Let all of this belong to one life. Let the adult self lead with love.”
new: Note: whenever I refer to the ‘subconscious’ I’m referring to all of the processes under the surface of your conscious awareness: perceptions, emotions, desires, avoidance tendencies, imagery, memories, body signals, habits, intuitions, automatic behaviours and so forth. You can work with all of these together as if it’s all one ‘mind’, or you can work with it as a set of parts, an ‘ecology’ if you like. There isn’t a ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ way to approach it. They’re all maps. Don’t form a priesthood around either one!
Working with parts: Precision. Working with Higher Self: Coherence. Doing both: Communion.
If you need to work with the ‘whole’, the subconscious as one:
a) ‘Invoke’ the subconscious in some way. Something simple like ‘Hello, wise subconscious…’ or whatever works for you.

If you need to work with the ‘ecology’ in the subconscious (child parts, protectors, ‘critic’, fantasy making parts, body memories, social part, spiritual part (God/source/best benefit of all beings part) ‘wiser’ part etc etc then:
a) It’s usually a good idea to start with unity. So ‘invoke’ your Higher Self: Hello my Higher Self/universal heart-mind/wise subconscious…
b) Move into differentiation. “Which part is afraid? Which part wants to protect you? Which part wants to avoid it? Which part knows what to do? Which part is too young for this?” Etc.

c) Move back into unity again. “And all of these parts are part of the one life, and as the adult in charge of this life you can lead with love, knowing that all of these parts are part of your life…” Etc.

old: Some people feel more fragmented when they begin by naming twelve parts and assigning everybody office space. Start with the sacred whole when that happens.

“I begin from the universal heart. I begin from Higher Self. I begin from the part of me that belongs to life before it belongs to any wound, role, family, group, identity, ideology, or story. Please help me understand what is true, kind, timely, stabilizing, and useful.”

If Higher Self, the universal heart, or any sacred language feels unavailable or borrowed from somebody else, begin with plain witnessing instead. Notice the room, the body, and the younger state. The fact that something can notice is enough adult presence for the first step.

If you can already notice and distinguish what is happening inside, you don’t need to keep rehearsing the Witness. Work with the warmth, protection, or direction that is actually missing. Higher Self language can help you gather around a meaningful source of care; it doesn’t establish that a perfectly capable inner parent is already available. Those adult functions still grow through practice.
Differentiate only when something specific appears:
“Is this the inner child?” “Is this a protector?” “Is this the body?” “Is this fear?” “Is this intuition?” “Is this social conditioning?” “Is this divine guidance, or my interpretation of guidance?”
Start from the heart. Differentiate only as needed. Return to the heart.
new: Sometimes, it’s better to start with the whole.

Some people make themselves too fragmented by starting to work with parts. ‘Here’s a part! Here’s another one! I’ll get twelve of them in a room and give them all an office to hang around in!’ So it’s better to start from the Sacred.

Start like this: ‘I’m approaching this from the universal heart. I’m approaching this from my Higher Self. I’m approaching this from the part of me that knows it belongs to life, not any wound, or role, or family, or group, or identity, or ideology, or story. So can you please tell me what’s going to be true and kind and timely and stabilising and useful here?’ Etc.

It can be that you can’t even access your Higher Self, or the universal heart, or whatever works for you. (Btw, if it doesn’t work for you don’t use it! It’s no good adopting somebody else’s map.) In that case, start by just witnessing whatever is coming up. Notice the room, your body, the fact that you’re in a younger state etc.

Once you have the ability to notice, and to differentiate, you don’t need to keep rehearsing it. Just work on whatever it is you need to work on (often warming up and protecting yourself and knowing what to do etc). So even though it can be useful to talk about your Higher Self, it doesn’t mean you already have all the good inner parenting functions etc that you need. You usually need to work on developing them.

Differentiate only as you need to. “Is this my inner child? Or is this a protector? Is this my body? Is this fear? Is this intuition? Is this my social part? Is this divine guidance, or is this my interpretation of divine guidance?”
Always start from the heart, differentiate when you need to, then come back to the heart again.

old: This guide doesn’t tell anyone to use substances. It does acknowledge that many people first encounter self-hypnosis, inner-child contact, or Higher Self dialogue while altered.
Do not use altered states to force revelation. Use them to deepen listening, strengthen love, and improve ordinary life.

A past opening can be a resource without becoming a state you must reproduce. Having experienced love once, being able to access it only in a particular state, and contacting it reliably in daily life are different things. Let the experience widen what seems possible while you build usable access. If the child cannot receive it, meet the difficulty rather than escalating the intensity.
During or after an altered state, these prompts are usually more useful than demanding a revelation:
“Help me stay grounded.” “Help me receive only what I can integrate.” “Help me remember love.” “Help me return when it is time.” “Help me translate this into one ordinary-life change.”
Don’t use self-hypnosis to prolong an altered state indefinitely, recover memories, intensify fear, bypass sleep, override medical needs, or make yourself less able to communicate.
If the state makes you less loving, less grounded, less honest, less able to sleep, less able to communicate, or less able to meet ordinary responsibilities, stop deepening and start integrating.
new: NB: I am NOT saying use these. However, many people attempt to do things for the first time such as self hypnosis, contact with their inner child, contact with their Higher Self etc when they are in a mind altered state.
If you do use them, be aware you don't want to force a revelation out of the state but instead use it to help you do things in your regular life.

If you have had an opening in the past, the key is to recognize that it is different to have an experience, access it in a particular state and access it in your day to day life. It is great that it has opened but if the child can't take it in, then

Use phrases such as; Help me to ground. Help me to only take that which I can take in. Help me to remember love. Help me to come back when the time is right. Help me to take one change into my regular life.
You should NOT use self hypnosis to; Keep you in that state forever Get memories to come up Make yourself afraid to do things Not sleep Override things that your body needs Not talk to people

If you are doing this in an altered state of consciousness and it is helping you not to love, not to ground, not to be honest, not to sleep, not to communicate, not to do regular life things, you need to STOP trying to go deeper and work on integrating what you have.

old: Self-hypnosis can become very powerful during loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, sexual energy, prayer, sleep loss, or other plant-medicine-adjacent states. Sometimes the mind opens faster than the adult self can organize what is arriving.

Intensity then gets mistaken for meaning. Sometimes the inner child is finally speaking. Sometimes a Protector is showing fear, or shame, grief, anger, longing, and other buried material are asking for care. But an intense state can also be bodily overload, environmental chaos, sleep deprivation, or plain confusion. A frightening image isn’t automatically truth, a bad feeling isn’t automatically a lesson, and a “download” doesn’t deserve belief merely because it came with excellent lighting.
Before trying to interpret the state, ask a simpler question:
“What kind of problem is happening?”
new: Self hypnosis can be extremely powerful when you are in a different state of consciousness (such as on loveyhuasca, meditating, in a lucid dream, when you are grieving, when you are using sexual energy, when you are praying, when you are not sleeping, or with other plant medicines etc). Sometimes you can open your mind up faster than you can process it as an adult.

The problem comes in when people are in a different state of consciousness, they think it must mean something. Sometimes it is your inner child, sometimes it is a Protector projecting their fear, sometimes it is your shame/grief/anger/longing etc coming up for help, but sometimes it is just your body's way of saying it doesn't like what is happening, the environment is chaotic, you didn't sleep well, or for any number of other reasons it might not make sense. Just because you get a picture that scares you, it might not be true. Just because you have a bad feeling, it doesn't mean it is a lesson. Just because you get a download in nice lighting, that doesn't mean you should believe it.
Instead of trying to interpret what is going on, ask yourself;
“What kind of problem is happening?”

old: Daydreaming can be intuition, simulation, grief digestion, creative rehearsal, symbolic teaching, or the subconscious showing a possible future, fear, or desire. It can also become avoidance, fantasy addiction, dissociation, romantic obsession, or an escape hatch from adult life.
Does the daydream return me to life with more clarity, love, and action? Or does it pull me away from life into repetition, craving, and avoidance?
When it seems useful, ask:
“What is the guidance inside this?”
When it seems to be pulling you away, change the body before debating the story. Sit upright. Open the eyes a little. Feel the feet.

“Subconscious, thank you for showing me images. If this daydream is useful, please reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, please bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with in a gentle but structured way.”
Then get embarrassingly practical:
“What real-life action is this daydream replacing?”

The answer may be: send the message, stop sending the message, clean the room, eat, sleep, grieve, create, apologize, leave, tell the truth, make the plan, ask for help, return to the task, or stop chasing unavailable love.
new: Sometimes daydreaming is something that your subconscious mind is doing to help you. It is simulating an idea or event to help you digest grief or teach you something. The very act of daydreaming may be helping you to access your creativity or allowing your subconscious to show you a potential future. Sometimes your subconcious will show you things that you may be afraid of. Sometimes it will show you what you want.

Other times daydreaming may be taking you away from your life in a detrimental way. It may be that you are escaping reality and are addicted to fantasies rather than the real life. You may be dissociating or obsessing about romantic partners or escaping from being an adult.

How do you know which it is? Simply ask yourself if the daydreaming is taking you closer to life, with more clarity, love and ability to take action or if it is taking you away from life, in a repetitive and craving way that takes you away from living your life.
If it is helping you then simply ask yourself what the guidance is and how you can use it.

If it is taking you away from life then change your body position, open your eyes and ask your subconscious to help you. Simply say to yourself, “Dear subconscious if what you are showing me is helpful then please also show me the helpfulness in it. If what you are showing me is a way of avoiding dealing with life then please show me in a gentle but structured way how to deal with life as it is right now.”
Then ask yourself what it is that you need to do in “real” life that you are avoiding by daydreaming.

You may need to send a text message or stop sending text messages. You may need to clean up your room, eat, sleep, deal with grief, create, apologize, leave, tell the truth, make a plan, get help, get back to a task that you were supposed to be doing, stop chasing love that is not available to you etc.

old: Use the Inner Signal app to get voice hypnosis sessions, learn the method, develop your own language, reflect on what you report, and ask questions about a hypnotist’s approach. Self-hypnosis doesn’t require an app, and finding a practitioner is an option rather than a graduation requirement.
new: You will need to download Inner Signal App for voice hypnosis, information, to learn the language, and for feedback on what you report. Have fun. Feel free to ask any questions you might have about what the hypnotist is doing. Self hypnosis is a great tool, but you don't need an app to do it. You may want to find someone, but it is not required to graduate.

old: Use self-hypnosis as a relationship with yourself. When the situation needs actual care, the guide shouldn’t become a substitute for it.

Get urgent help now for immediate danger, severe confusion, inability to keep yourself safe, or concerning physical symptoms such as chest pain or fainting. New or worsening suicidal thoughts, severe insomnia, mania-like or psychosis-like symptoms, or dissociation that disrupts functioning need prompt professional assessment, not a four-to-twelve-week practice schedule.

For ordinary learning, start with shorter sessions, warmth, a manageable subject, and a full return. Over a week or two, track one target—anxiety, daydreaming, relationship repair, an avoided task, sleep, emotional regulation, or intuitive accuracy. Worsening function or growing certainty about unverifiable memories calls for reassessment, not more intensity.
Seek suitable ongoing help for recurring panic, compulsive behavior, substance-related destabilization, or major relationship instability.
new: Remember, this is self-hypnosis, a relationship with yourself. If the situation calls for support, this guide isn't the right thing.

If you need help now: You may need help now if you feel in imminent danger, very confused, or unable to take care of yourself. You may need help now if you have physical symptoms (chest pain, fainting, etc.) You should seek professional help promptly if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, severe insomnia, new or worsening symptoms of mania or psychosis, or if dissociative symptoms are affecting your functioning. These are not problems that this guide will resolve in 4-12 weeks.

You probably don't need any more support than this: If you keep the practice shorter, make it warm, pick a small and tractable subject, make sure you come back out, and then see how it affects a specific target (anxiety, daydreaming, helping a relationship, facing a task you've been avoiding, helping you sleep, being less reactive emotionally, improving your intuitive accuracy, etc) for a week or two, and don't notice that your functioning is getting worse, or that you're getting more certain about unconfirmable memories, then you're probably doing fine.
You probably need more support if: You are experiencing recurring panic attacks, compulsions, substance destabilization, major relationship instability, etc.

old: Use a trauma-informed clinician trained in the method, present with you, for deliberate trauma-focused regression, searching for unknown traumatic origins through an affect or somatic bridge, or work with substantial flashbacks or dissociative reactions. A bridge follows associations from a feeling or sensation; regression revisits recalled or imagined younger experience. Either can have different uses, including resourcing. Ask what is intended and how uncertainty and unexpected reactions will be handled. Hypnosis cannot prove a historical event, even with a clinician present.

Trauma history, tears, or wanted difficult feelings don’t automatically exclude self-practice. Choose the working range with attention to the actual response and available support. Some people need a narrow range; others much broader. Confidence alone doesn’t supply missing support.

Major trauma guidelines emphasize treatments such as trauma-focused CBT variants, CPT, PE, and EMDR depending on the person and guideline. Self-hypnosis and inner-child practice may support that process, but high-risk trauma work needs a larger container.

If the practice makes ordinary life more loving, honest, functional, relational, grounded, and precise, continue gently. If it makes ordinary life less stable, stop deepening and return to sleep, food, grounding, boundaries, and outside support.
new: If you want to deliberately do trauma-focused regression (going backwards in your memory or imagination to times when you were younger), or affect and somatic bridging (following associations from an emotional or somatic experience to find the origin of that experience, particularly if it was a traumatic experience you don't know about), or if you find that you're having substantial flashbacks or dissociative reactions, then you should do this with a trauma-informed trained person present. It's best if they're trained in the specific method you want to do. Ask any potential person what they would do and how they deal with uncertainty. Note that even if you work with a person, hypnosis is not a way of knowing what did or did not happen to you. (Both regression and affect/somatic bridging can also be used to find resources and do other things, of course.)

Note that having experienced trauma, crying, and even wanting to feel difficult feelings, are not necessarily signs that you need more support than working on your own. You get to pick how wide and narrow a range you want to work in, but be aware that different people need different ranges. Pay attention to how you respond and what support you have. Feeling like you are handling it isn't a substitute for having support.

Note that many guidelines for treating major trauma recommend one or more of trauma-focused variants of cognitive behavioral therapy (sometimes called cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, eye movement desensitization and reprocessing, etc). Depending on the guideline and your situation, it may recommend one or the other or both. These can include self-hypnosis and inner child work. If you're working with high-risk trauma, you need a bigger container.

Always keep in mind that your functioning in ordinary life is the feedback. If you find yourself more loving, more honest, more functional, more relational, more grounded, more precise, etc. than when you started this process, keep on keeping on. If you notice that your ordinary life is becoming less stable, don't try to go deeper. Go for more sleep, more eating, more grounding, more healthy boundaries with other people, more getting support from other people, etc.

old: Do not treat inner voices, images, autonomous movements, or body signals as commands or proof. Listen, then reality-test.
new: DO NOT: View these experiences as anything but internal happenings that need to be reality tested at all times.

old: Do not chase grand downloads or turn demons, jinn, and “Unattached Burdens” into a hobby. Stabilize first, and seek help when reality-testing or function weakens.
new: DO NOT: Engage in seeking “downloads” of information or become obsessed with demons/jinn/Unattached Burdens or the like, until you have stabilized your life, perhaps even getting help to do so, if you are not reality testing well, or not functioning well in your life.

old: Do not use self-hypnosis while driving, bathing, swimming, operating equipment, supervising children, or doing anything that requires active attention.
new: DO NOT: Participate in self-hypnosis while operating a car, bathing, swimming, operating any equipment, supervising children, or engaged in any activity which requires active attention.

old: Do not force memory recovery, use trance to prove what happened, or suppress medical symptoms.
new: DO NOT: Attempt to “force” memories, to use trance to “prove” something happened to you, or to not get medical attention for symptoms, because you can “force” them down using hypnosis.

old: Do not override hunger, fatigue, pain, grief, anger, or fear before understanding the signal.
new: DO NOT: “Force” yourself to ignore your body’s needs, such as eating when hungry, resting when tired, responding to pain, etc., or your emotions, such as letting yourself grieve when someone dies, feeling anger when it is appropriate, acknowledging your fears, etc., until you know more about what the signals are telling you.

old: Do not prolong altered states indefinitely or treat intuition as fact without testing it.
new: DO NOT: “Extend” the duration of altered states indefinitely or accept “hits” of intuition as “real” without reality testing them.

old: Keep the inner roles in proportion: the child does not lead adult life; the Protector cannot exclude all love; the Nurturer cannot erase consequences; the Leader cannot bypass the child; analysis and tenderness both remain available.
new: DO NOT: Allow various internal roles to get out of proportion (e.g., allow the “Inner Child” to run your adult life, the “Protector” to preclude all loving relationships, the “Nurturer” to disregard consequences to others, the “Leader” to ignore the needs of the “Child”). You are capable of analysis, as well as tenderness.

old: Do not use NLP to override protectors, manufacture certainty, manipulate anyone, or perform healing when the body says no.
new: DO NOT: Utilize NLP techniques to “force” down “protectors,” to give yourself certainty you do not have, to manipulate others, or to “heal” yourself when your body is telling you not to.

old: Doubt, distraction, resistance, silence, and “no” do not prove that an induction is working.
new: Don’t consider negative indicators (doubt, distraction, resistance, lack of response, saying “No”) as good signs that the induction is working.

old: “The unconscious will keep me safe” does not replace clear limits, a safe setting, the ability to stop, and a tested exit.
new: Don’t rely upon the “safety” of “your unconscious mind” as the only safety factor in any session. Be sure you have set up clear limits, are in a safe place, and have a way to terminate the session and “get out” which has been tested and proven to work.

old: Ordinary sensations do not prove hidden trauma, illness, toxicity, possession, attachment, transformation, or subconscious truth.
new: Don’t believe that normal physical sensations are indications of hidden trauma, illness, toxins in your body, possession, “attachments,” “transformations,” or information from your “subconscious mind.”

old: Imagined repair does not establish physical recovery, neurological repair, cellular change, or a cure.
new: Don’t believe that anything is “healed” in your body (neurologically, cellularly, etc.) simply because it is “healed” in your imagination.

old: Do not install hidden instructions, undisclosed third-party activation, compulsory behavior, identity switching, or amnesia. A consciously chosen reusable cue should have a clear purpose, remain reviewable, and be retired if it becomes unwanted; saying “cancel” does not guarantee instant erasure.
new: Don’t put “hidden ‘commands’” in yourself, nor allow anyone to do so. Even if you are consciously placing something in yourself which you wish to utilize later, be sure that you know exactly what you are doing and why you are doing it, and be sure that you CAN “take it out” if you decide that you no longer wish to use it. It may not be as easy as simply saying, “Take out.” Nor should you allow anyone to activate these “commands” in you without your knowledge, to make you do something you don’t want to do, to make you into someone you don’t want to be, to give you amnesia, etc.

old: End every waking session with ordinary identity, movement, orientation, judgment, and a direct statement that the session has ended.
new: DO bring yourself completely back at the end of every “waking” session, declaring that the session is over.

old: Altered-state rule: do not ask for hidden truth while medically unsafe, panicking, sleep-deprived, nauseated, destabilized, manic, psychosis-like, or chemically overwhelmed. First stabilize. Truth that requires destabilization is not ready to be known directly. Ask for capacity, not content.

Sometimes it feels as though the subconscious knows something the conscious mind can’t yet tolerate. The subject may be sexuality, grief, trauma, family truth, betrayal, shame, vocation, relationship reality, illness fears, spiritual calling, addiction, identity, or moral conflict.
Interrogation is the dangerous response:
“Tell me now.” “Reveal everything.” “Stop hiding.” “I demand the truth.”

That pressure can produce flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, or a generally worse Tuesday. Flooding can make the adult capacities needed for pausing, comparing options, reality-testing, planning, and choosing much harder to reach. In that state, regulation and support come before deeper dialogue. Silence may be protection when the adult lacks enough regulation, support, humility, or practical capacity to receive the material.
Ask for the next tolerable piece:
“Do I need to know the content now, or do I need to build capacity first?”
“What would make the conscious mind 5% more able to receive this?”
“Can you show me the truth as a symbol, not a full revelation?”
“Can you give me the next protective action without revealing the whole story?”
“Who, if anyone, should help me hold this?”
A safer script:

“Wise subconscious, if there is something I cannot yet handle, please do not break it open violently. Help me become someone who can know it safely. Give me preparation before revelation. Give me grounding before memory. Give me support before intensity. Give me one next action.”

Hypnotic imagery can be meaningful without being literal. The mind symbolizes, compresses, distorts, dramatizes, and borrows from culture and fear. Around trauma and memory especially, treat an image as an image and involve outside support when needed.
new: NOTE: If it is not medically safe, or if you are panic stricken, sleep deprived, nauseated, deeply destabilized, manic, psychosis like, or chemically overwhelmed, do all you can to stabilize and then ask for what your subconscious needs you to know. It is not ready for you to know if you need to destabilize to know what it is! Ask for capacity and not content!

What to do if your Subconscious Mind Knows Something You Don’t Want to Know. It may have to do with your sexuality, a grief, trauma, family issue, betrayal, shame, vocation, relationship, medical issue, spirituality, addiction, identity, moral issue, or whatever.
Don’t bully your subconscious mind into telling you what it is by saying things like:
Why won’t you just tell me? What are you hiding? Tell me right now! I command you to tell me what it is!

This usually leads to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, and a really, really bad day. If you are flooded, then you can’t use your adult capacities to be able to consider different options, to reality test, to plan, to choose differently. Work on your regulation and get support before proceeding. The subconscious may be silent until your Adult is able to regulate, get support, be humble, and proceed in a way that does not blow your Adult out of the water. Ask the parts what they need for your Adult to be able to know what it is:

Do I need to know what it is, or do I need to work on capacity? What can be done to make my conscious mind 5% better at knowing what it is? Can you tell me what it is in a symbolic way without full revelation? Can you tell me what to do to be safe without telling me what it is? Do you need me to get support in order for you to tell me what it is? If so, what kind of support? Who can I go to?

Consider saying: “Dear Subconscious Mind, you are wise and you know things that my conscious mind is not able to know yet. Please don’t rip the bandage off. Prepare my conscious mind to know what it is in a safe way. Ground me before showing me a memory. Support me before turning up the intensity. Tell me what to do next so that I can be ready for what you want me to know.”

REMEMBER: Just because you see something in a hypnotic state does not mean that it is literally true, especially when it comes to traumatic memories. The mind often makes images that are meaningful to you, but are symbolic. It often squashes several things together, distorts, dramatizes, and pulls from cultural sources. Just because you see it, doesn’t mean it’s true. Get support outside to help you!

old: Use the same practice rather than learning a second script: gather attention, listen, respond, wait, return. Fifteen minutes is a convenient appointment with yourself, not a therapeutic dose or a timetable your feelings must follow. Use a few minutes to enter, leave several minutes to return, and let the middle unfold at its own pace. Five minutes of silent listening is available when useful; you can interrupt it to change direction.
new: Notice there is no need to learn a second script! The process is the same. You are simply practicing for fifteen minutes or so. That is long enough to induce yourself (it only takes a few minutes), practice for a short time (five minutes is plenty to see what happens when you simply sit in silence, listening, and you can interrupt yourself at any time to change direction if that feels better) and come out again (that takes a few minutes too).

old: Another simple entry is to notice three things you see, three you hear, and three bodily sensations; then two of each, then one. Count from five to one and begin listening. Use the entry that suits you, rather than stacking inductions.
new: You can also try other ways of inducing yourself such as becoming aware of 3 things you can see, 3 things you can hear, 3 things you can feel in your body; then 2 of each, 1 of each, counting from 5 to 1 and beginning to listen. Choose one way to induce yourself, you don't need to try all of them! (In fact, it might be counter-productive!)

old: After familiar runs, shorten a recording to the cues you still need, then try practicing without playback. Keep recordings when you enjoy them; independence means being able to guide yourself, not having to refuse help. The optional re-entry cue can shorten an already familiar induction.
new: Once you have practiced listening a few times with the recordings, you may want to shorten them to speed up your induction, or even practice without playing them back at all. On the other hand, if you like using the recordings, there is no reason to stop! Being able to guide yourself does not mean you have to! (NB. You may wish to use the following to help you re-enter your process, this will also shorten your induction if you already know what to do.)

old: Afterward, ask what needed warmth, what needed protection, and what direction serves truth, love, and life. Was there something to explore, or capacity to build? What can you carry yourself now? When action is needed, make it concrete: “If [cue] happens, then I will [small action].” Check how you sleep, relate, and function later, not only how impressive the session felt.
new: As you come out of the process ask yourself what you learned needed warmth, what needed to be protected, what you need to do differently to be more in accord with truth and love and life. Is there something you want to explore more fully or a capacity you want to build? And most importantly, what can you carry with you as you move forward from this? If you identified something you needed to do differently, make a plan with yourself to do that thing. The more specific you can be, the more likely you are to change: “If _________ (fill in the cue for the old pattern), then I will do ________ (fill in one small action that will begin to change the pattern).” Then check back later and see how you are doing – sleeping, relating, functioning, etc.

old: Sit rather than lie down when you tend to daydream, dissociate, or fall asleep. Let the spine rise without becoming military, soften the jaw, and keep some awareness of the room. Save lying down for sleep, deep rest, or dream incubation.
“I am not leaving life. I am listening more deeply to life.”
Begin by invoking the larger field:

“Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious, body intelligence, inner child, inner adults, protective parts, and all that serves truth and love: please help me understand what I need to know, only in the form and timing that is useful, kind, stabilizing, and real.”
You’re asking the conscious mind to listen without forcing an answer.

Thoughts do not have to stop before deeper listening begins. Let thoughts, sensations, images, doubts, and emotions pass through awareness without fighting or following them; keep the intention lightly in the background and notice what becomes salient on its own.
“Please tell me what I need to know, or ask what you need to know. I will wait silently for five minutes.”
The response may be a phrase, sensation, memory, color, child, protector, pain, warmth, silence, task, gratitude, an urge to stop, or the realization that today’s practice is over.
Listen to all of it. Believe none of it automatically.
new: Note: If you have a tendency to day dream, dissociate or fall asleep, it is better to do this exercise sitting up until you are ready to try this lying down, either to go to sleep, get a very deep rest or incubate dreams. If you are sitting, keep your spine straight but not rigid like a soldier. Relax your jaw and stay somewhat connected to the room you are in.
“Unless I’m going to sleep or want deep rest, I am not leaving life; I am listening more deeply to life.

I invoke my Higher Self, universal heart-mind, wise subconscious mind, intelligence in my body, inner child(ren), inner adult(s), protector(s) and all that is of truth and love to help me know what I need to know in a form and at a level that will be useful, kind, stabilizing and real for me.”
Ask your conscious mind to listen.

This does not mean you have to stop thinking to listen. Just notice your thoughts, body sensations, pictures, doubts, emotions, etc. Don’t fight what comes up, but don’t go with it either. Just notice what stands out on its own as you hold the idea of what you are doing in the back of your mind.
Internally say, “Tell me what I need to know or ask me what you need to know and I’ll sit in silence for 5 minutes and listen.”

You may hear a phrase, feel a body sensation, notice a memory, see a color, be contacted by a child or protector, feel pain, warmth, complete silence, know that you need to do something, be grateful for something, feel you need to stop the listening or any number of things.
Listen to everything and believe nothing.

old: Reverse whatever you used to enter. If you floated, regain chosen weight. If you became small, return to ordinary scale. If you met a younger state or several parts, confirm present wholeness, body ownership, and adult judgment. If you traveled, come back by the same route. Keep only the qualities you deliberately chose.
new: Make sure that you come out of the session in reverse to how you got in. If you floated up, float back down the same way and come back down to your chosen weight. If you shrank yourself, make sure that you come back to your normal size. If you went inside to a younger you or parts of you make sure that you know that you are whole now, in your body and with your adult judgement. If you traveled somewhere, come back the same way. Only bring back what you need to bring back.

old: “I bring back only what is useful now. The rest can remain safely held until there is more capacity. I return to the room, the body, the day, and one honest action. All instructions to deepen or remain in this session are finished. I keep only the ordinary-life intention or future-practice cue I consciously chose; neither keeps today’s altered state running. I am myself, in my body, with adult judgment fully available.”
new: You may want to say something like, "I am only bringing back what I need to bring back at this time. Anything that is not needed by me at this time I will store away safely until such time as I need it. I am coming back now to this place, to my body and to normal day to day living, to doing one honest action at a time. Any instructions that I gave myself to go deeper or to remain in session are now over. (Unless you are giving yourself instructions to implement in ordinary life or to cue practice at a future time, and those instructions should not take you out of ordinary life.) I am me now, in my body, with my adult judgement."

old: One — feel the body’s contact and chosen weight. Two — let the breath return to its ordinary rhythm. Three — hear the room and name where you are. Four — move fingers, toes, shoulders, and eyes. Five — eyes open, present, ordinary, clear. The session has ended.
new: Then you might want to count yourself out. "1 I am coming back now into my body, to my chosen weight. 2 I am coming back to my normal breathing pattern. 3 I am hearing the sounds around me now, I am in (where ever you are). 4 I am moving my fingers and my toes, my shoulders and my eyes. 5 I am opening my eyes now, feeling normal and present. My session is over."

old: Name the day or date. Look left, right, near, and far. Move before standing, and stand only when steady. Check that you are actually oriented and alert; repeating the count is not proof of a complete return. Note only what actually appeared, and any action it calls for. Then do something normal.
new: When you come out make sure that you come all the way out. State to yourself what day it is or what date it is. Look to your left and to your right. Look at something close and something far away. Move about a little bit before you stand up, and only stand up when you feel that you can do so. Make sure that you are alert and oriented. Just because you counted, doesn't mean that you are all the way out. Take note of what you need to do as a result of the session, if anything, and then go about doing something normal.

old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.
new: In the event that a recording that you are listening to stops, you can say to yourself that the recording has stopped and the session is over and use the above mentioned method to bring yourself out of the session. Open your eyes, state to yourself where you are and what day it is, push down with your feet or your hands, move about, look around and then use the above mentioned 5 step method to bring yourself out. Don't sit there waiting for the recording to "let you out" it isn't going to.

old: Sleep is separate. A sleep recording may end in sleep or quiet rest. A waking recording shouldn’t end by preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, an undefined reset word, or an invitation to remain altered indefinitely.
new: NOTE: If you are using a recording to take you to sleep, it is all right to allow the recording to put you to sleep or to allow you to remain in a quiet place. But if it is a recording to be used while awake, it should not put you in a role, it should not take away your judgement, it should not inhibit your movement capabilities, it should not leave you blank, it should not leave you with an undefined reset word and it should not allow you to remain in an altered state for as long as you wish.

old: Sometimes the inner-child question lands nowhere because a private self had very little room to develop. In controlling families, rigid religions, enmeshed communities, or high-pressure achievement systems, performance can begin so early that a person doesn’t know what they feel, want, believe, or prefer until somebody else tells them first. Then “love yourself” produces a reasonable question: love whom? Reparenting and identity-building can proceed together. For some people the child-self is already easy to feel. For others, creating enough safety for preference, curiosity, and experimentation is part of how that self becomes easier to hear.
This may apply when:
You do not know what you want unless someone else says what they want first.
Your opinions shift dramatically depending on who is in the room.
You agree in the moment and later realize you did not agree.
You feel responsible for other people’s emotions to the point of self-erasure.
Self-love feels performative.
The question “What does my inner child feel?” produces guesses, not felt answers.
You can rebel, but you cannot yet choose.

A useful developmental explanation is that when childhood is organized around avoiding pain and preserving attachment, attention goes into reading danger, meeting expectations, and keeping the bond. That can leave less room for the ordinary experiments that answer, “What do I like? What do I want to try? Who am I when nobody is grading me?” This is a practical model, not a claim about one specific brain system.

Sometimes a temporary, intentional period of distance from the people or group supplying the answers helps quieter preferences surface. Use that distance only long enough to tell your own signal from the social echo; prolonged isolation would undermine the purpose.

The difference between a human doer and a human being helps here. When worth isn’t felt internally, it gets earned through beauty, performance, intellect, status, spirituality, or becoming indispensable to everybody else. Those can all be real gifts. They become belonging bargains when failure in the arena feels like losing yourself.
Useful questions:

“What do I like when no one is watching?” “What do I believe before I check whether others approve?” “What do I want that is neither rebellion nor compliance?” “Where am I buying belonging with self-betrayal?” “Which arena am I using to earn the right to belong?” “What would I try if nobody needed to be impressed?” “Which relationships let me remain myself?” “What am I noticing in my body, and what meaning am I giving it?”

Give the inner child a small experiment with no résumé value: painting, dancing, gardening, a language, a sport, volunteering, music, or anything else you’re allowed to be bad at. The inherited parent may demand immediate talent. The adult can answer, “We’re finding out whether we enjoy this, not proving our worth.” Give it enough repetitions to get past the humiliation of being a beginner.

For a child, belonging can feel like survival, so families, religions, romances, political tribes, spiritual groups, institutions, and online communities can reach astonishingly far into identity. Adulting means noticing where you buy belonging with self-betrayal, choosing your own ground, and learning that you can disappoint someone without disappearing. The subconscious contains a crowd of borrowed voices, which is why this belongs in a self-hypnosis guide.
“Where do I become less true in order to remain included?”
“What would belonging look like if I did not have to disappear?”

“Is this guidance, or is this a belonging program?” “Is this love, or is this fear of exclusion?” “Is this conscience, or is this conditioning?” “Is this devotion, or is this compliance?” “Is this rebellion, or is this freedom?”
Then wait for the body. It isn’t infallible, but it deserves a seat at the hearing.
new: It can be difficult to connect with your inner child if your inner child didn’t have the opportunity to develop. This happens often when you grow up in a situation where you don’t have a private self, for example when your family, religion, or community ‘takes over’ very early in your life. Or you are pushed to achieve very early in life. The result is that you don’t know what you feel, what you want, what you believe, what you like and dislike until you have heard someone else’s opinion about it. If you are in that situation, it can be difficult to follow the advice to ‘love yourself’. You don’t even know who ‘yourself’ is! So you need to do reparenting and finding yourself in parallel. For others, it is very easy to work with the inner child, they can feel it easily.
You are in this camp if:
You don’t know what you want, until you have heard what someone else wants.
Your opinion is very different when you are with different people
You agree with people at the moment but when you are by yourself you realize that you don’t agree with them
You take responsibility for the emotions of others, at the expense of yourself
When you try to love yourself, it feels more like a show
When you try to find out how your inner child feels, you feel that you are guessing instead of feeling
You can rebel, but you can’t choose

This happens because when you were a child, you didn’t have the opportunity to explore what you like, what you want to try out and who you are. This is not a criticism of your brain but a practical way to look at it.

Sometimes you need to distance yourself for a certain time from the people or group that you normally get your answers from. But not for too long, as then you defeat the purpose of this exercise! You need to differentiate yourself a bit from your social environment.

What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. In these areas, you made a bargain with yourself that as long as you are good in these areas, you will be good enough.
So in order to find yourself, you can ask yourself:
What do I like when nobody is looking?
What do I believe when I don’t check with other people?
What do I want that is neither in rebellion nor in compliance with others?
Where am I buying my sense of belonging at the expense of betraying myself?
In what arena am I trying to buy my sense of belonging?
What can I try on that I don’t need to be good at?
With whom can I be myself?
What do I feel in my body and what do I make out of it?

Give your inner child the opportunity to do something that has no value on its own and that it doesn’t need to be good at for its resume. For example painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, playing a sport, doing volunteer work, playing a musical instrument, etc. Because often your inner parent tells your inner child that it is supposed to be good at something as soon as it starts doing it. And that’s not good because your inner child will get humiliated that it isn’t good at it. So try things out long enough until the humiliation is gone.

When you are a child, you will feel that you need to belong to a family in order to survive. That is why many people do things for their family, their religion, their romantic partner, their political tribe, their spiritual group, their institution or their online community that they otherwise wouldn’t do! Part of adulting is finding out where you sell yourself in order to belong, and then making the conscious choice where you want to belong. Because a large part of your subconscious mind, is made out of other people. This is why you are reading a self hypnosis guide!
Where am I betraying myself in order to belong?
What does it feel like to belong without betraying myself?
Where do I think I am following my own guidance, but I am in fact following my belonging program?
Where do I think I am doing things out of love, but I am actually doing it out of fear of not belonging?
Where do I think I am listening to my conscience, but I am actually listening to my conditioning?
Where do I think I am doing something out of devotion, but I am actually doing it out of compliance?
Where do I think I am rebelling, but I am actually free?
And then look what your body tells you. It is not always correct, but it is a good place to start.

old: Once or twice a week, give the same practice more time when that is useful. More time needn’t mean greater intensity. Start from Higher Self or neutral witnessing, follow what appears, borrow an adult function when needed, and ask whether anything important is being bypassed. Leave room for the full exit and any ordinary action needed afterward.
new: It’s good to do this once or twice a week, though more is fine. It doesn’t have to be very intense but it is good to start from Higher Self or at least a neutral witnessing place. It’s also good to bring in some adult function to make sure nothing is being bypassed and so that at the end of the exercise, when the experience is over, there is the possibility of coming out completely and doing whatever normal thing needs doing.

old: Do the ordinary action immediately when possible. That teaches the subconscious that the adult heard and acted, instead of staging another beautiful internal meeting and then leaving the dishes exactly where they were.
new: If possible, it’s good to do the normal thing immediately after the exercise, so that the subconscious sees that the adult’s actions have been heard. Otherwise, the dishes won’t get done.

old: “Syncing the hemispheres” can be a useful description of how the state feels, but I wouldn’t turn it into literal neuroscience. A large resting-state fMRI study of 1,011 people didn’t support the pop-science picture of whole people being globally “left-brained” or “right-brained,” even though particular functions and networks can be lateralized.
new: I use the expression ‘syncing the hemispheres’ but don’t want to over interpret what is going on neuroscientifcally. A huge study of resting state fmri scans of 1011 people does not support the common pop neuropsych notion that people in general are left or right brained. But there is evidence for lateralisation of some functions or networks.

old: You’re inviting the verbal, analytical, imaginal, emotional, somatic, intuitive, relational, and spiritual modes to cooperate. Nobody needs to win a hemisphere election.
new: Let’s elicit a high level of co-operation between the verbal, the analytical, the imaginal, the emotional, the somatic, the intuitive, the relational, the spiritual … It’s not an electoral process. Nobody needs to win!

old: The loving mind stays warm while the analytical mind stays bright. The intuitive mind offers signals without becoming dogma. The rational mind tests signals without killing them. The body gives yes, no, and not-yet. The imagination opens the field. The adult self chooses the next real action. Peace and precision become compatible.
new: The mind of love and the mind of analysis can BOTH be there - warmth and brightness. The mind of intuition and the mind of rationality can BOTH be there - intuitive signals and testing of those signals without dogma or killing them. The body can have a voice - saying yes or no or not yet. The imagination can have opened up the field and then the adult can choose what to do next in the real world…. It can be peaceful but also precise.

old: Love can drift into fantasy without analysis. Analysis can become sterile without love. Intuition can become delusion when nothing tests it; testing can become dead when nothing intuitive is allowed to speak. Let the modes correct each other.
new: Without the mind of love the mind of analysis can be sterile. Without the mind of analysis the mind of love can lead to fantasy. Without testing intuitive signals they can become delusions. Without intuitive signals the testing can be dead. So these ‘modes’ can correct each other.

old: A powerful state matters only if something survives it: kinder behavior, more humility, better judgment, real service, or a more workable ordinary life.
new: And it’s got to lead somewhere!

old: Clinical caution still matters. Mayo Clinic warns that hypnosis used around stressful earlier-life events can trigger strong emotional reactions, and that other treatments may fit historical trauma work better.
new: The Mayo Clinic warns that using hypnosis to deal with earlier life stressful events may invoke strong emotions and that there are other types of treatments that may be more helpful with historical trauma.

old: Use self-hypnosis for regulation, dialogue, reparenting, clarity, habit change, present safety, emotional integration, and ordinary-life action.
new: DO use Self Hypnosis to help you: regulate your self, talk to your self, re-parent your self, gain clarity, change habits, make your life safer in the now, integrate emotions, and take action in ordinary life.

old: Do not use it to force trauma memories, prove what happened, suppress medical symptoms, destabilize yourself, or replace appropriate clinical care.
new: DO NOT use Self Hypnosis to help you: force yourself to remember trauma, force yourself to “prove” trauma through memories, suppress medical symptoms, de-stabilize your self, or NOT seek correct treatment.
